symptoms: The failure names a table and happens at resolution time
The table is visible in the console of the catalog service and not to the job
The same job resolves other tables in the same database
likely_causes: The session catalog is not the catalog that holds the table
The table exists in another account and is reached through a resource link that is missing or named differently from the source resource
The identity running the job cannot describe the table, and the catalog answers as if it did not exist
diagnostic_steps: Read the catalog dump for the table name exactly as the query writes it, including the database qualifier
Read the catalog configuration of the session: a table that resolves under one catalog name and not under another is not a missing table
When the table belongs to another account, read whether a resource link exists and whether it carries the same name as the source resource
fixes: Qualify the table with the catalog that holds it, or point the session at that catalog
Create the resource link for the cross-account table, with the same name the source resource has
Grant the identity the permission to describe the table, when the catalog is hiding it rather than missing it
unsafe_fixes: Creating a table with the same name in the local catalog, which makes the name resolve to different data
Granting broad catalog permission to make the object visible, when the precise fix is one grant on one resource
verification: Re-run and confirm the table resolves, then compare the row count and the schema with the source: a name that resolves to the wrong table also stops failing
rollback: Restore the previous catalog configuration or query text. A resource link that was created can be removed, and doing so restores the previous resolution for every consumer of that link
